# Class handle forms a verification library relies on

The task module runs every fixture through the public CLI in both HDL optimizer
modes on legacy, compact/portable and compact/GMP values. Expected outputs were
checked against an independent industry-standard simulator; the clause lines
below are from `SystemVerilog-1800-2009.txt`. Behaviour the text does not settle
is recorded in `docs/lrm_decisions.md` (S11-D5 to S11-D8).

| Fixture | Clause and oracle |
| --- | --- |
| `call_sources` | 6.24.2 L7430-7431: "When called as a task, $cast attempts to assign the source expression to the destination variable. If the assignment is invalid, a run-time error occurs, and the destination variable is left unchanged." L7433-7435: "When called as a function, $cast attempts to assign the source expression to the destination variable and returns 1 if the cast is legal." Method calls, static calls, virtual results and a conditional as source; class array elements and `ref` formals as destination. |
| `element_targets` | 6.24.2 L7433-7435 as above; 8.9 for static properties. Destinations through nested containers, records, class properties, computed receivers and `$`; casts in `while`, `for` and `?:` conditions; a suspending task and a forked block. |
| `string_values` | 6.24.2 L7437-7438: "It is important to note that $cast performs a run-time check. No type checking is done by the compiler, except to check that the destination variable and source expression are singulars." A string destination takes a string; every other source fails. A string source converts to a packed value (6.16) and never to a real or a non-member enum value. |
| `handle_outputs` | 13.5: output, `inout` and `ref` formals of handle type bound to elements of containers, records and classes, from statement calls and from calls used as values. |
| `call_formals` | 13.5: a function returning a handle takes packed, string, real, array, container, enum and record `output`, `inout` and `ref` formals. |
| `handle_conditionals` | 11.4.11 L15147-15148: "If cond_predicate is true, the operator returns the value of the first expression without evaluating the second expression; if false, it returns the value of the second expression". L15205-15207 for the class result type. Comparisons of method results with `null` and with each other (11.4.5, 8.4). |
| `discarded_pops` | 7.10.2 (queue methods): `void'(q.pop_back())` and a statement `q.pop_back()` of a handle queue; methods of handle elements (8.4). |
| `unformatted_handles` | 21.2.1 L35884-35887; decision S11-D8: `$swrite`, `$swriteh`, `$swriteb`, `$display` and `$write` of a class handle with no format. |
| `class_string_actuals` | 13.5.2 L19103-19104 applies to `ref`; 13.5 for `output` and `inout`: class string properties as actuals of `output` and `inout` formals, by bare name, through `this` and through a handle. `$swrite` into a class string property. A `case` on a string method result compares as strings (Str1 == Str2, 6.16). |
| `subroutine_records` | 13.5.2 L19103-19105: "Arguments passed by reference shall be matched with equivalent data types (see 6.22.2)." Two-state record locals of class methods as `ref` and `const ref` actuals; a declaration initialized from a whole record element of a queue or associative array, in a task, a function and a procedural block. |
| `function_fork_locals` | 9.3.2 L11480-11481: "Variables declared in the block_item_declaration of a fork-join block shall be initialized to their initialization value expression whenever execution enters their scope and before any processes are spawned." Handles declared in a `join_none` branch of a function belong to the activation: two activations keep their own. A formal the branch captures is a `$cast` source. |
| `fixed_local_locators` | 7.12.1 L9293-9295: "max() returns the element with the maximum value or whose expression evaluates to a maximum." Locator methods of a fixed array local of a subroutine, including descending and ascending declared ranges, signed and 4-state elements. |
| `bits_replication` | 11.4.12.1 L15266-15267 and 20.6.2 L34593-34594: "The $bits system function returns the number of bits required to hold an expression as a bit stream." `$bits` of types and fixed-size variables in a replication constant, inside and outside subroutines. |
| `constraint_scope` | 18.9 L30749-30750: "The constraint_mode() method can be used to control whether a constraint is active or inactive." `this.c.constraint_mode` and a bare constraint name, own and inherited, set and read in functions and a task. |
| `handle_call_arguments` | 11.4 L15727: "A function call is an operand." 13.5.1 L19086: "Pass by value is the default mechanism for passing arguments to subroutines." A call that returns a handle as the handle argument of another call, inside methods, tasks and functions; the inner call keeps its depth relative to the enclosing function. |
| `string_contexts` | 11.4 L15727: "A function call is an operand." A string function with a real argument; a string function result as an associative key and as a random state inside a function; a formatted real nested in a string concatenation or conditional (21.3.3). |
| `nested_string_keys` | 7.8.2 L8658: "Associative arrays that specify a string index have the following properties". 11.4 L15727: "A function call is an operand." A nested associative array and a record element of a string-keyed array, both indexed by a function result inside a class method. |
